  "title": "Federation for organization, repositories and users",
  "body": "See https://owncloud.org/features/federation/\r\n\r\nI would like to see a feature like the federation feature of next cloud. It gives the ability to share repositories, organizations or users between multiple Gitea instances.\r\n\r\nThis has the advantages that business users could share their projects with other companies. This feature would reduce the management and administrativ overhead.\r\n\r\nThis makes it easier for beginners to start with Gitea.\r\n\r\nIt could uses the \"Mirror\"-feature of Gitea.",

      "body": "@strk I agree with the idea to split this thing into many tickets. This ticket might be the user federation ticket doesn't it? But I don't want authentication for users of other platforms. I want the ability to add other users. The user will receive an invite from the user's Gitea instance. He will access the repository or organization from the his instance. "

    {
      "id": 297375409,
      "url": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/1612#issuecomment-297375409",
      "created_at": "2017-04-26T11:47:42Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Granting permissions to someone in a federation requires being able to\nidentify that someone (a global address). As you mentioned owncloud I\nthink owncloud uses \"<user>@<domain>\" as the identifier, but I dunno what\nprotocol it uses for that. Friendica/GNUSocial and other OStatus implementing\nfederations can also use \"<user>@<domain>\" mapping to something else via\nthe Webfinger standard (which is open as to allow for specifying different\nprotocols). Another community (the IndieWeb one, see indieweb.org) uses\nweb addresses to identify people, as it's used with OpenID up to version 2.0.\nNew OpenID (OpenID-Connect) uses again Webfinger.\n\n"
    },

      "updated_at": null,

    {
      "id": 311613823,
      "url": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/1612#issuecomment-311613823",
      "created_at": "2017-06-28T09:56:55Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "Regarding \"what standard do we want to choose\" I just want to point you to [ActivityPub](https://activitypub.rocks/ ) which is currently being finished by the Social Federation working group of the W3C. Some project implementing it (or currently working on that) are pump.io, Mastodon and MediaGoblin.\r\n\r\nThey don't use WebFinger though as they dislike the idea of a fixed .well-known path, but there are [ideas about interoperability](https://github.com/w3c/activitypub/issues/194 )."
    },
    {
      "id": 368599184,
      "url": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/1612#issuecomment-368599184",
      "created_at": "2018-02-26T18:25:11Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 14",
      "body": "This feature will be truly game changer; keybase.io recently came out with client side encrypted git, thats also interesting."

    {
      "id": 382876960,
      "url": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/1612#issuecomment-382876960",
      "created_at": "2018-04-19T20:51:58Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 15",
      "body": "Just want to point out that [ActivityPub](http://activitypub.rocks) is now done. \r\n\r\nAdding support for AP would make Gitea compatible with a growing number of federated servers, such as Mastodon, PeerTube, NextCloud and HubZilla, broadening its reach considerably, not to mention a standout differentiator against GitLab. \r\nIt would also have the potential to dethrone GitHub as the go-to hosting for open-source projects, since most are here for the community pull request workflow that AP would allow in a decentralised manner, increasing privacy and eliminating a single point of failure for a large percentage of the free software community. \r\n\r\nAnyway, my hope is this gets implemented, it has the potential to be revolutionary! "
    },

"

      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "Would be awesome if we could have different projects discussing a common implementation of the ActivityPub protocol (ie using the same extension for verbs, etc). This would enable users of gitea, gogs and gitlab to work together seamlessly just like users of various social media platforms that federate can discuss seamlessly.\r\n\r\nCould this be the place? -> https://github.com/git-federation/gitpub"

      "url": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/1612#issuecomment-395022241",
      "created_at": "2018-06-06T10:31:26Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-06-06T23:45:22Z",
      "author": "Participant 20",
      "body": "This would be amazing! I think Nextcloud (/Owncloud) is the perfect example of how this could work with the ideal implementation, as @JonasFranzDEV suggested.\r\n\r\nWith Nextcloud, if I want to share a folder with a user on another instance, I can easily do so and setup a shared folder across both instances.\r\n\r\nIf I could do that for a repository hosted on my Gitea instance, granting a user on another federated instance access to the repo, with that repo then appearing in their Gitea interface with full ability to interact with issues etc (with some clear denotation in the UI that this repo was hosted on another instance), that would be pretty amazing.\r\n\r\nThe goal being discussed to adopt a shared standard between Gitea and other open source self-hosted projects (such as GitLab CE) definitely makes sense, and it would be great if this was adopted allowing federation between Gitea, Gogs, GitLab, etc.. Migrating from GitHub for private projects is easy with nothing really lost, but for public open source projects we need to acknowledge a big benefit of GitHub is the community. I've discovered a lot of projects actually on GitHub. If there was some way of federating popular projects, users activity feed (i.e. being able to follow a friend on another instance and follow their activity, liked projects, with privacy settings taken into account etc) would be excellent - if that would be possible.\r\n\r\nFederated pull requests would be a great first step towards this (#184), and likely the most crucial missing feature at the moment."

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "I'd just like to add that before Microsoft inspired a mass migration away from Github this wouldn't have been a killer feature... NOW it is. Less and less of the repos for OS projects that I'm researching are on Github now (MAYBE mirrored here). \r\n\r\nI've read that ones Github commit history can read like a cv and that one of the reasons that the software world is so career mobile is that a person can self-teach valuable skills, EASILY DEMONSTRATE them (public github history), and thus qualify for better earnings/etc. If your contribution history is spread out over dozens of private servers it is FAR less visible/useful.\r\n\r\nAlso, any of those servers could go down at any time and that part of your history is now gone. A proper implementation of federated repositories would mean that I could participate in dozens of projects on dozens of instances (from my instance) and if they ALL went down I'd still have my 'federated git profile'."

    {
      "id": 585700496,

    {
      "id": 683213233,
      "url": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/1612#issuecomment-683213233",
      "created_at": "2020-08-29T01:27:15Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 8",
      "body": "Perhaps, for a simple implementation, gitea could run an [ipfs](https://ipfs.io) node in the background hosting local repository files (using [ipns](https://docs.ipfs.io/concepts/ipns/) to point to the latest versions of the repositories). We could then have a simple [gossip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gossip_protocol) protocol implementation to find other gitea instances and get ipns hashes & preliminary data (stars, name).\r\nThe benefit to using ipfs would be when users on one instance want to view or fork repositories on other instances, it would contribute to hosting parts of that repository and make accessing the repo faster for network as a whole.\r\n\r\nUsing ipfs/ipns could also be used for distributing user data such as starred repositories, pull requests, bio, etc. each node would only store names & ipns hashes for users on other networks that the instance cares about and it would be trivial to request profile data for unknown users.\r\n\r\nipfs already has a go [implementation](https://github.com/ipfs/go-ipfs) and for instance discovery something like [this](https://github.com/hashicorp/memberlist) could be used."
    },
    {
      "id": 683223821,
      "url": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/1612#issuecomment-683223821",
      "created_at": "2020-08-29T02:37:20Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 9",
      "body": "There is no requirement for peer-to-peer storage here, what you describe doesn't seem required or even related to the problem at hand. I don't think there's interest in moving away from the Git storage format and transfer protocol. Maybe you should open a separate issue if you see a benefit here (I certainly don't)."

    {
      "id": 683300624,
      "url": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/issues/1612#issuecomment-683300624",
      "created_at": "2020-08-29T14:48:11Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 8",
      "body": "> There is no requirement for peer-to-peer storage here\r\n\r\nI think gitea would benefit greatly from peer-to-peer sharing of repositories so that popular repos would be redundant in the case of instances going down. While someone can just mirror a repository to their own instance, it would fragment the development of a project if there is no central place to commit to. If the git protocol was layered on IPFS, it would allow for deduplication when forking projects on a single instance (so an entire copy wouldn't have to be stored). \r\n> what you describe doesn't seem required or even related to the problem at hand.\r\n\r\nThe reason federation is so useful (and why people want it so much) is that it allows collaboration across instances. The InterPlanetary Name System (IPNS) has identical behavior to OpenID because it can be used to identify a user who has permission to update certain data (e.g. their repositories and personal profile). An IPNS address could uniquely identify a user from another instance without necessarily having to tie that user to a specific instance. Lets give an example:\r\nAlice is self-hosting an instance of gitea at aliceland.net\r\nWhen Alice creates a new account, gitea would create an empty profile, host it on IPFS and then generate a unique IPNS address that points to that profile. Whenever Alice creates a new repository or updates her profile in any way, gitea will (behind the scenes) create a new IPFS record, unpin the old one, and reassign Alice's IPNS address to it.\r\nNow lets say Bob wants to submit a merge request from his mirror of the repository on bobland.net to aliceland.net.\r\nWhen Bob originally forked Alice's repo to bobland.net he made a note of the IPNS of Alice's repo as well as the IPFS location of the commit he forked from.\r\nWhen Bob wants to open a merge request, he writes his message and then bobland.net will put the following things in an IPFS block:\r\n- Bob's IPNS user address\r\n- The IPFS address of the commits Bob wants to pull in\r\n- The IPFS address of the commit in Alice's repo that should be modified\r\n- Bob's Messsage and Title for the merge request\r\n- Signature of data with Bob's private IPNS profile key\r\n\r\nBobland.net will then send the IPFS address to aliceland.net which can then choose to totally ignore it, OR parse the address, verify the commits, create a IPNS address for the comment thread (that points to all the comments) and then notify Alice that some guy named Bob on instance Bobland.net has sent a merge request for 3 commits over IPFS. The comments would also be hosted over IPFS and accessible via an IPNS address.\r\nThis pattern of using IPNS for mutable data (like a comment thread) and IPFS for immutable data (like comments and commits) can be applied for most inter-instance federation.\r\n>I don't think there's interest in moving away from the Git storage format and transfer protocol.\r\n\r\nThis approach to federation wouldn't have to move away from the Git format. [Git can simply be layered and stored on ifps](https://docs.ipfs.io/how-to/host-git-style-repo/) (while also taking advantage of deduplication). Git's Merkle Tree system doesn't necessarily have to be integrated with IPFS's (although that would be cool) and the git transfer protocol would still be the same, IPFS would just moderate the communication between instances."
    },
